old: Somebody warded a way out of here before the passage was ever choked. The vein through it is the same coin-gold as the stones above.
new: A way out of here, warded into the stone before the passage was ever choked. The vein through it is the same coin-gold as the stones above.

old: The rubble gives at your push — someone's already cleared a path through. The old gallery beyond is dark, but it is open.
new: The rubble gives at your push; the path through it was cleared before you got here. The old gallery beyond is dark, but it is open.

old: Rubble and worked stone choke a passage that clearly led somewhere once. Someone sealed this side deliberately, and not long ago either.
new: Rubble and worked stone choke a passage that led somewhere once. The stones sit in courses, and there is barely any dust on them.

old: A carved shape crouches against the far wall, limbs folded, its eyeless face turned to the floor. It has not moved since you noticed it. That is the only reason you are still standing here.
new: A carved shape crouches against the far wall, limbs folded, its eyeless face turned to the floor. It has not moved since you noticed it.

old: You keep your distance. Whatever wakes it, you would rather not be the one who finds out.
new: You keep your distance. The eyeless face stays pointed at the floor.

old: The doorway you came through, seen from the inside: the runes run the same order on this face, which means they were cut to be read from in here. Somebody expected to be standing where you are.
new: The doorway you came through, seen from the inside: the runes run the same order on this face. They were cut to be read from in here.

old: A waist-high plinth of the same pale stone as the ruin's, and the same hand's runes wrapped twice around it. Every line points inward. Whatever it holds, it was built to keep holding it.
new: A waist-high plinth of the same pale stone as the ruin's, and the same hand's runes wrapped twice around it. Every line points inward, and none of them come back out.

old: Not a prisoner. An ANCHOR — a twin to the stone the Horns hauled out of the ruin, and it has been drinking the ward's slow pour for three centuries to stay awake. Pisces, hoarse: "This is why the Door works at all. Somebody left it something to come home to, and then somebody sealed the room and let it drink."
new: Not a prisoner. An anchor: a twin to the stone the Horns hauled out of the ruin, and it has been drinking the ward's slow pour for three centuries to stay awake. Pisces, hoarse: "This is why the Door works at all. Somebody left it something to come home to, and then somebody sealed the room and let it drink."

old: Someone knelt here long enough to cut a tally into the floor slab, and long enough after that to stop.
new: A tally cut low into the floor slab, close in against the wall. It stops well short of the corner.

old: Rubble and old wardwork still choke this side passage. Whatever's back there can wait until the main halls are actually safe.
new: Rubble and old wardwork still choke this side passage. It can wait until the main halls are clear.

old: [Rope Work] — You make the line fast to the stub, drop the tail across, and set it taut. The crossing is a crossing now, and it stays one.
new: [Rope Work] — You make the line fast to the stub, drop the tail across, and set it taut. The line holds your weight and stays where you put it.

old: You get a hand on the stub and lean out. Nothing about that gap is jumpable, and nothing about the stub is climbable. What it wants is a rope.
new: You get a hand on the stub and lean out. The gap is too wide to jump and the stub too smooth to climb; what it wants is a rope.

old: The floor stops. You put a boot to the lip and gravel goes over the edge and keeps going. Not without something to hold.
new: The floor stops. Gravel goes over the lip when your boot finds it and keeps going, and you are not crossing that without a line.

old: A strapped case set down against the wall and never picked up again, the leather gone stiff and pale. Whoever put it there meant to come back through the span.
new: A strapped case set down against the wall and never picked up again, the leather gone stiff and pale.

old: The straps give at a pull. Inside: chalk, a bent square, a coil of good wire, and five gold in a twist of cloth that somebody was saving for the walk home.
new: The straps give at a pull. Inside: chalk, a bent square, a coil of good wire, and five gold in a twist of cloth.

old: The flagstone gives half an inch under your hand. Somewhere close, something CLICKS. Nothing else happens. This time.
new: The flagstone gives half an inch under your hand. Somewhere close, a catch clicks. Nothing else happens.

old: A narrow slit runs along the wall at knee height, primed and waiting. This wants a careful, deliberate touch, not a shove.
new: A narrow slit runs along the wall at knee height, primed and waiting. A careful, deliberate touch could still it.

old: The floor ahead looks perfectly ordinary. Something about it still itches at the back of your mind.
new: The floor ahead looks perfectly ordinary. You do not have the eye to check.

old: You look again, and this time you see it: the grain runs the wrong way, and no dust has settled in months. That is not floor. That is a very good painting of floor.
new: You look again, and this time you see it: the grain runs the wrong way, and no dust has settled in months. What you are looking at is a very good painting of floor.

old: The floor ahead looks exactly like the floor behind you. Somehow, that is the part that bothers you.
new: The floor ahead looks exactly like the floor behind you. An eye trained to look properly would find the difference.

old: The stone here looks like all the other stone. It is not.
new: The stone here looks like all the other stone. Without a reading for mana, that is as far as you get.

old: Something under the stone hums off-key. Eyes that read mana could say what.
new: Under your boot the stone hums off-key. Eyes that read mana could say what.

old: You give the wire a wide berth. Something in the dark past it has not noticed you yet.
new: You give the wire a wide berth. Nothing past it in the dark has noticed you yet.

old: A coil of taut wire lies strung ankle-height between two stones, near-invisible against the dust. Whatever it is rigged to is worse than a stubbed toe.
new: A coil of taut wire lies strung ankle-height between two stones, near-invisible against the dust. The far end disappears into the dark.

old: Whatever waits beyond this arch, you are not walking into it yet — not with the halls still armed, not without the Horns at your back.
new: The halls are still armed, and the Horns are not with you. Both have to change before you go through this arch.

old: The hall ends in a sealed archway, and beyond it something vast fills the dark almost completely — the same shape you glimpsed crouched near the entrance, closer now, utterly still. It is not still the way a statue is still.
new: The hall ends in a sealed archway. Past it the dark is filled nearly to the edges by the same shape you glimpsed crouched near the entrance, closer now and holding still. There is no dust on it.

old: [Detect Magic] — Wardwork, and awake. It does not flare and settle the way a bound ward should. It holds one low steady note, like a breath nobody has to let out, and you have felt that note somewhere else.
new: [Detect Magic] — Wardwork, and awake: it does not flare and settle the way a bound ward should. It holds one low steady note, like a breath nobody has to let out, and you have felt that note somewhere else.

old: [Observe] — Worked stone, deliberate, and not one line of it reads like a lock. Whatever this door is for, it is not keeping people out. You would have to stand here longer, with someone who knows more than you do.
new: [Observe] — Worked stone, cut deliberate. Not one line of it reads like a lock, and nothing here tells you what it is for.

old: [Observe] — You take the runes in order, the way you would read a sentence. The turns repeat at a fixed interval. The pantry frame does exactly that, at exactly that interval, and this one is worn deeper: it has been doing it longer. Behind you, Pisces says nothing, which from him is applause.
new: [Observe] — You take the runes in order, the way you would read a sentence. The turns repeat at a fixed interval. The pantry frame does exactly that, at exactly that interval, and this one is worn deeper: it has been doing it longer. Behind you, Pisces says nothing.

old: The runes are the same. Not similar — the same hand, the same order, as the door in the inn's pantry.
new: The runes are the same. The same hand, the same order, as the door in the inn's pantry.

old: Pisces reaches the door before you do and stops a handspan short of it. "The same hand. Not a school, not a fashion. A HAND, and it cut this one first." He does not look away while he says it.
new: Pisces reaches the door before you do and stops a handspan short of it. "The same hand. One person's work, and this door was the first of it." He does not look away while he says it.

old: Pisces steps back at last. "It is not a lock. The lines run one way, they have run one way for a very long time, and something on the far side has been drinking the whole while. Your inn has a frame by this hand. Sleep well."
new: Pisces steps back at last. "The lines run one way. They have run one way for a very long time, and something on the far side has been drinking the whole while. Your inn has a frame by this hand. Sleep well."

old: An alcove beside the sealed door, and something standing in it: ward-stone, shoulder-high, cut in the same hand as the runes. It is not a statue. Statues are not built facing the door they guard.
new: An alcove beside the sealed door, and something standing in it: ward-stone, shoulder-high, cut in the same hand as the runes. It is not a statue.

old: A ring of fire-blackened stones, the ash inside long dead and cold. Something sat here in the dark and knew how to keep a fire — or learned how, the way they say these things learn, when the moon is full and their minds come clear.
new: A ring of fire-blackened stones, the ash inside long dead and cold. Raskghar keep a fire when the moon is full and their minds come clear; this ash is layered, lit and relit.

old: A fire-pit ringed with blackened stones, its ashes cold. Whoever tended it had hands enough to strike a spark, and left gnawed bones banked around the edge, cracked for their marrow.
new: A fire-pit ringed with blackened stones, gnawed bones banked around the edge and cracked open for their marrow. Nothing in the ash has been warm for a long time.

old: A midden of cracked bones, marrow sucked clean. Gnoll, most of them. A few too large to name. They have been sorted, almost stacked, as though something down here counts its meals and keeps the score.
new: A midden of cracked bones, marrow sucked clean. They have been sorted by size, almost stacked. Gnoll, most of them; a few too large to name.

old: A heap of gnawed bones, splintered for their marrow. Some are Gnoll. One is a Drake's. They are stacked, not scattered. And that is worse than if they had been.
new: A heap of gnawed bones, splintered for their marrow. Some are Gnoll. One is a Drake's.

old: Two of them crouch where the tunnel narrows, moon-grey and mountain-shouldered, knuckles to the stone. Their small eyes track you without blinking. Between you and the deeper dark, they are the door — and the lock.
new: Two of them crouch where the tunnel narrows, moon-grey and mountain-shouldered, knuckles to the stone. Their small eyes track you without blinking. Behind them the tunnel keeps going down.

old: The gallery floor slopes down past where the den used to be, into a chamber someone else has clearly been surveying.
new: The gallery floor slopes down past where the den used to be. You come out in the delve's staging chamber.

old: Claw-gouges score the pillars, going quiet toward the back. The den is empty — cleared, then sealed. Whatever the warren was, it is a grave and a door now.
new: Claw-gouges score the pillars, going quiet toward the back. The den is empty — cleared, then sealed.

old: Sinew and bone hooks, strung low across the gallery floor. It has the shape of something meant to catch. You don't know how to spring it safely.
new: Sinew and bone hooks, strung low across the gallery floor. You don't know how to spring it safely.

old: You've picked this snare clean today. The warren restocks on its own schedule.
new: You've picked this snare clean today. Nothing has been re-rigged since.

old: Sinew and bone hooks, strung low across the gallery floor. Whatever set it hunts down here, same as you.
new: Sinew and bone hooks, strung low across the gallery floor. Trained hands would start with the hooks.

old: A length of wire runs low across the passage, pinned to a rusted stanchion. Whatever it's meant to catch, you can't tell how to spring it safe.
new: A length of wire runs low across the passage, pinned to a rusted stanchion. You can't tell how to spring it safe.

old: Wire, taut and low, strung off a rusted stanchion. Something in the nest rigged this. Careful hands could clear it.
new: Wire, taut and low, strung off a rusted stanchion. Careful hands could clear it.

old: Bone and wire, tangled at the drain mouth. It has the shape of a trap. You can't read it well enough to touch it — that's trap-craft, a rogue's trade.
new: Bone and wire tangled at the drain mouth, in the shape of a trap. You can't read it well enough to touch it — that's trap-craft, a rogue's trade.

old: You work the bone pins loose and unwind the wire. A few coins sit wedged in the silt beneath it, dropped by whoever it once caught.
new: You work the bone pins loose and unwind the wire. A few coins come loose from the silt beneath it.

old: A little iron strongbox, silt-caked, dragged here by someone who never came back for it.
new: A little iron strongbox, silt-caked, dragged into the nook and left there.

old: A market crate, swollen and burst, washed down through a grate above. Whatever was in it fed something down here long ago.
new: A market crate, swollen and burst, washed down through a grate above. Nothing left inside it but silt.

old: [Appraise Foe] — You lie flat on the ledge and read the nest like a map. Two sentries on the silk, a brood-hollow behind them, and a tunnel dropping away toward the Dungeon proper. That's where the rest of them are. Count, size, exits: you have it all, and you never had to draw a blade.
new: [Appraise Foe] — You lie flat on the ledge and read the nest like a map: two sentries on the silk, a brood-hollow behind them, and a tunnel dropping away toward the Dungeon proper. The rest of them are down that tunnel.

old: The floor gave way here, not long ago: a raw crack breathing air colder and older than the sewers ever hold. The claw-scores on its lip all point one way: down. Something climbed up through this, and means to again.
new: The floor gave way here, not long ago: a raw crack breathing air colder and older than the sewers ever hold. The claw-scores on its lip all point one way: down.

old: A fresh fissure splits the sewer floor, exhaling a dry, breathing cold from far below. Deep gouges rake the stone lip. Something big has been using this as a door.
new: A fresh fissure splits the sewer floor, gouges raked deep into the stone lip. Something big has been using it as a door. A dry cold breathes up out of it and does not stop.

old: East past the gate road, across the floodplains — this is the ruin. Survey stakes, a banked fire, and someone's washing on a line: the Horns got here first. The sealed level is deeper in, under the pedestal court.
new: East past the gate road, across the floodplains — this is the ruin. Survey stakes, a banked fire, washing on a line: the Horns got here first. The sealed level is deeper in, under the pedestal court.

old: Cold stone, unlit. The spiral wants something the press alone doesn't give.
new: Cold stone, unlit. The press alone does not wake it.

old: "Good," she says, once, and goes back to the rope. From Yvlon that lands about like a hand on the shoulder.
new: "Good," she says, once, and goes back to the rope.

old: Three coils of rope laid out in exact parallel, and an Antinium re-counting them, because the count is the point and the rope is only the rope.
new: Three coils of rope laid out in exact parallel, and an Antinium re-counting them.

old: Spoil from the gap, sorted into two heaps: worked stone in one, plain rubble in the other. Somebody is keeping every piece a chisel ever touched.
new: Spoil from the gap, sorted into two heaps: worked stone in one, plain rubble in the other. Every piece a chisel ever touched is in the first.

old: Broken stone, sorted by whether anyone shaped it. The carved heap is the smaller one and by a long way the tidier.
new: Broken stone in two heaps, worked and unworked. The worked heap is smaller, and still being added to.

old: Good rope, dry, coiled by somebody who has watched bad rope let go.
new: Good rope, dry, and not a frayed strand in it.

old: The string is taut. Somebody re-tensions it each morning, which is not a thing four adventurers usually bother to do.
new: The string is taut. The knot at each stake has been retied more than once.

old: Cold days ago. They struck the camp properly, filled the pit, and took the rope with them. Whatever the Horns came down here for, they carried it home.
new: Cold days ago. They struck the camp properly, filled the pit, took the rope. Nothing left but the ring of stones.

old: Banked low and fed on whatever burns down here. Somebody turns it every few hours; the ash is raked, not spilled.
new: Banked low and fed on what burns down here. The ash lies raked in a ring, and the coals are still working.

old: A cookfire kept small on purpose, ringed with stones somebody carried in. It has been burning longer than a day.
new: A cookfire kept small on purpose, ringed with stones carried in from outside. It has been burning longer than a day.

old: The sentinel's face is gone, but its posture survives: shield toward the court, warning anyone who follows its gaze.
new: The sentinel's face is gone. The posture survives: shield raised toward the court.

old: A stone rests in a shallow cradle atop the plinth, held there by nothing you can see. Something older than the dust stands close enough to notice you noticing.
new: A stone rests in a shallow cradle atop the plinth, held there by nothing you can see.

old: Below the pedestal: not treasure. A DOOR — unhung, unmarked, utterly ordinary except that four adventurers go silent around it at once. Ceria, finally: 'That's wardwork. Old, fed wardwork. We're taking it home.' The anchor stone comes up with it.
new: Below the pedestal: not treasure. A door, unhung, unmarked, utterly ordinary except that four adventurers go silent around it at once. Ceria, finally: 'That's wardwork. Old, fed wardwork. We're taking it home.' The anchor stone comes up with it.

old: The stone doesn't move. Whatever holds it there is still standing guard, close enough that reaching for it feels like a very bad idea.
new: The stone doesn't move. It does not even shift in its cradle, and the court has gone very quiet.

old: Both spirals hold their light, and the seam under the plinth stops fighting your hand. Whatever the ward was keeping out, it was never the plates — it was whoever hadn't walked them. Ceria, already reaching for rope: 'Ksmvr. Down. Carefully.'
new: Both spirals hold their light, and the seam under the plinth stops fighting your hand. The ward wanted the plates walked in order, and now they have been. Ceria, already reaching for rope: 'Ksmvr. Down. Carefully.'

old: A carved socket in the ruin stone. Whatever sat here, someone carried it off.
new: A carved socket in the ruin stone. The hollow is clean-cut and empty.

old: [Detect Magic] — You read the binding the way Pisces reads a page, and the reading is the undoing: the ward was keyed to whatever stood guard here, and a keyed ward answers anyone who can say the key back. The seal lets go. Ceria, from the gap: 'Do that again and I'm putting you on the ledger.'
new: [Detect Magic] — The ward was keyed to the guardian that stood here, and the key still works: the seal lets go. Ceria, from the gap: 'Do that again and I'm putting you on the ledger.'

old: The stone soldier still stands, and the cradle it stands over is empty. Whatever it was set here to keep was carried out past it and it did not move. A ward outlasts the thing it warded. That is the whole nature of a ward.
new: The stone soldier still stands, and the cradle it stands over is empty. The anchor stone was carried out past it and it did not move.
